We survey over 1,900 AI-tagged crypto projects, filter to investment-focused agents, and curate 10 representative projects spanning strategy and observability dimensions. case_studies.title: Certified Policy Optimisation for Nested Causal Bandits via PAC-Bayes Risk
case_studies.abstract: Critical sequential decisions are rarely single-timescale: a strategic decision causally shapes the context in which every subsequent tactical choice is made; standard bandit and reinforcement-learning theory does not capture this causal coupling between timescales. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of making sequential decisions in complex systems with causal relationships between different levels of decision-making. The authors built a new approach called Nested Causal Thompson Sampling (NCTS) to optimize decision-making in these systems. The result is a more effective way to make strategic and tactical decisions in nested causal bandit problems.

case_studies.abstract: Complex operational workflows coordinating personnel, tools, and information are central to system operations, yet end-to-end automation remains challenging due to extensive human input requirements and limited ability to adapt over time. The researchers built a system that operates in three phases to extract, execute, and evolve workflow graphs. case_studies.title: OmniVerifier-M1: Multimodal Meta-Verifier with Explicit Structured Recalibration
case_studies.abstract: Visual outcomes are increasingly central to multimodal large language models, making reliable and fine-grained verification essential for scaling generalist foundation models. In this work, we investigate multimodal meta-verification, which leverages verifier-generated rationales rather than decision-only signals, and explore how to effectively incorporate meta-verification feedback into multimodal verifier training. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of reliably verifying visual outputs in multimodal large language models by building a multimodal meta-verification system called OmniVerifier-M1, which resulted in more efficient and fine-grained verification. The system uses symbolic verifier outputs to improve verification accuracy. This is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.
